full_judgment:
3. The appellant's case in brief, that the Lackatorah Tea Estate is an old tea garden in Bangladesh established in 1880 under the Lackatorah Tea Company Limited for the purpose of planting, producing and selling tea. The said company has been possessing a big quantum of land including the land recorded under Mouza Lackatorah Tea Garden JL No.75 appertains to Khatian No.5, Plot Nos.735 and 737 measuring an area of 3.08 acres. The whole land of the said garden is an under exclusive possession of its Manager, staffs and all records of right, title and interest are duly made by the Government in the name of the appellant, and the said garden has been paying taxes regularly to the Government and earning a good amount of foreign currency. The respondent No.3 Syed Ullah was a peon of the Roads and Highways department, after retirement from service with an ulterior motive filed Title Suit No.24 of 1993 in the Second Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Sylhet in favour of a "mazar" named Sheikh Mizir Khasdabir's Mazar claiming title over 3.57 acres of land belonged to Lackatorah Tea State. The said suit was ultimately transferred to the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Sylhet and it was renumbered as Title Suit No.31 of 1999 and the said tea garden had been contesting the same. The said, Syed Ullah suppressing the fact of pendency of the said suit with a malafide intention filed an application before the Waqf Administrator of Bangladesh for enlistment of the land in dispute as Waqf property, and managed to get an order of enlistment in respect of 0.70 acres of land as Waqf Estate and also get permission to construct structures thereon. Thereafter on 5-6-1998 the said Syed Ullah alongwith others made attempt to construct a house in the suit land, but being resisted by the employees of the tea estate they failed. The said land enlisted as Waqf property is under absolute possession of the tea estate since 1880 and no mazar of anybody is there. It is further stated that before the Waqf Administrator in the aforesaid EC No.18130 the said tea estate filed written objection supported by all documents of title, but the administrator of Waqf illegally without considering of the facts by his arbitrary order declared 0.70 acre of land as "Waqf property". Hence, the said tea estate as plaintiff instituted the instant Miscellaneous Case No.29 of 2002 in the Court of District Judge, Sylhet. On transfer it was heard by the First Court of Additional District Judge, Sylhet who by the impugned judgment and order dated 15-6-2004 dismissed the case, and hence the appeal. 

 10. On perusal of the said order it appears that the said Miscellaneous Case was instituted by the National Tea Company and the Manager Lackatorah Tea Garden acted on its behalf. The allegations of the garden are that, the "Mazar" in question is not situated within the Lackatorah tea garden, in total 3.08 acres of land appertains to Plot Nos.735, 737 of Khatian No.5 was recorded in the name of Lackatorah Tea Garden since it was purchased by the tea company and the respondent No.3 Syed Ullah with an evil intention in collusion with the respondent Nos.1 and 2 got it recorded as Waqf property.
